info.title: Home display admin API
info.description: How the owner of a running server looks at it and changes it, from the same machine. Served over a local socket (a Unix domain socket in the PKI directory, mode 0600), not over the network. No endpoint returns a pairing code, a key or a certificate.

get.summary: Every display the server knows, by name.

200.description: The displays, with where each stands. Requests that lapsed are not listed.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

get.summary: One display and where it stands.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is known.

delete.summary:
Forgets a display, whatever its state, so it can ask again as if for the first time. A member that is forgotten
is turned away at once, whatever its certificate says.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

200.description: The display as it was, now forgotten.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is known.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

post.summary: Approves a display that is waiting, because the code the owner read off its own panel matches.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

requestBody.description: The code from the display's own panel.

200.description: Approved. The display becomes a member the next time it asks.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

403.description: The code does not match what the display would show. The display stays as it was.

404.description: No display of that name is waiting, or its request lapsed.

409.description: The display is not waiting for approval.

429.description: Too many wrong codes were typed for the display in a row, so none is looked at for 15 minutes, the right one included. The message says for how long.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

put.summary:
Gives a display a layout: from its next check-in it is sent that one when it doesn't ask for another itself (a
`layout` in its own request wins). Any display the server knows can be given one, approved or not.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is known, or no such layout.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

delete.summary: Takes a display's chosen layout away, so it is sent the default again.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

200.description: The display, with no layout of its own.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is known.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

post.summary:
Turns a waiting display down, until it is forgotten. For a member with another key waiting to take its name,
turns that key down and leaves the member as it was.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is waiting, or its request lapsed.

409.description: The display is not waiting for approval.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

post.summary:
Ends a member's membership. It is turned away on its very next request, whatever its certificate says, and
cannot renew.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The display's name, as `displays` lists it.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: No display of that name is known.

get.summary: Every viewer, oldest first, with where each stands. Nothing here can be used to sign in.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

post.summary:
Makes a viewer: someone who may look at the picture in a web browser, and the link that signs them in. The link holds a
one-time code, which is shown here and nowhere else, and works once, within the time given.

requestBody.description: What to call it, and what it may see.

200.description: The viewer, and its link. The link is not shown again.

400.description: The request could not be used. `code` says why.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

404.description: A layout asked for does not exist.

409.description: There are as many viewers as there may be.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

delete.summary: Forgets a viewer altogether, which frees its place. Its token, if it had one, stops working.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The viewer's id, as `viewers` lists it.

200.description: The viewer as it was, now forgotten.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

post.summary:
Ends a viewer's access at once, whatever state it is in: a link not yet used stops working, and a token stops being
accepted at its next request. The viewer stays listed, as revoked, until it is forgotten.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The viewer's id, as `viewers` lists it.

500.description: The server failed. The log has the detail.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

schema.description: The answer to a request that failed.

ApiError.description: The answer to a request that failed.

ApproveRequest.description: What the owner read off the display's own panel.

code.description:
The pairing code on the display's own panel: twelve letters and digits, in any case, with or without the
dashes. `I` and `L` are read as `1` and `O` as `0`. Type it from the panel, never from anywhere else: the
server does not show it, because a code copied from the server would say nothing about the display.

ChooseLayout.description: The layout to give a display.

DisplayEntry.description:
A display the server knows, and where it stands. Nothing here is secret: it never carries a pairing code, a key
or a certificate.

name.description: The name the display gives itself.

waiting_since.description:
When the request that is waiting was made: the display's own request to join, or (for a member) another
key's request to take its name. A request lapses a day after this if nobody answers it.

certificate_not_after.description: For a member, when the latest certificate it was given ends.

certificate_expired.description:
A member whose certificate has run out. Nothing to fix: it gets a new one by itself, with no one at the
server, the next time it is switched on.

changing_keys.description: A member that has been given a certificate for a new key and has not used it yet.

replacement_waiting.description:
A different key is waiting for the owner to approve it taking this member's name, as when a display was
reflashed and lost its key. The member carries on meanwhile.

oneOf.description:
What the display said it is when it last asked: its model, panel, image formats and firmware. Self-asserted: for
the owner to see before approving, never a reason to approve.
What the key that is waiting to take this member's name says it is, if there is one and it said.

layout.description:
The layout the owner chose for this display, which it is sent when it doesn't ask for one. Left out, it gets the
default layout.

DisplayState.description: Where a display stands. A name appears here as soon as it asks to join.

message.description: For a person to read. Its wording may change; act on `code`.
examples: minutes must be a whole number from 1 to 240

ErrorCode.description: Why a request failed, for a program to act on.

IssueViewer.description: What a viewer is asking of the server to be: the label the owner will know it by, and what it may see.

label.description: What to call it, from 1 to 40 characters: "kitchen tablet".

layouts.description: The layouts it may look at, by name. Left out or empty, all of them.

lifetime_days.description: How long its token lasts once the link is used, from 1 to 3650 days. Left out, 90.

code_minutes.description: How long the link works, from 1 to 1440 minutes. Left out, 15.

refresh.description:
Give it short-lived access tokens (an hour, unless `[server.web] access_token_minutes` says) and a rotating refresh
token to renew them with, in place of one token that lasts `lifetime_days`. A token that is lost is then good for an
hour and not a quarter of a year, and a refresh token that is copied is noticed, which ends the session. `lifetime_days`
is then how long the session lasts.

default.description: The layout a display with none chosen is given if the schedule doesn't say otherwise.

current.description:
What a display with none chosen is sent now: the default, unless the layout schedule says another for this
time.

LayoutList.description: The layouts a display can be given.

OpenWindow.description: How long to open the pairing window for.

minutes.description: Minutes from now, from 1 to 240. Opening an open window again sets the time afresh.

ProfileStatus.description:
What a display said it is when it asked to join: its model, panel, image formats and firmware. Self-asserted, so it is text
for the owner and never a reason to let a display in.

formats.description: The image formats it can decode.

ViewerEntry.description: A viewer, as the owner sees it. Nothing here can be used to sign in.

id.description: What to give `viewer revoke` and `viewer forget`.

scope.description: What it may look at: `layout:*`, or `layout:NAME` for each layout.

refreshing.description: Whether it has short-lived access tokens and a refresh token, and not one token that lasts.

link_expires_at.description: For one waiting, when its link stops working.

expires_at.description:
Once signed in, when its access ends: for a plain viewer, when the token runs out, and for a refreshing one, when the
session does (its access tokens run out and are renewed all the time).

last_used_at.description: When it was last used, to within ten minutes or so.

ViewerIssued.description: A viewer made, with the link to sign it in. The only answer of this API that holds a secret, and it is shown only now.

code.description:
The one-time code, which a browser exchanges for a token. It is in `link`; it is here for a program that builds its
own.

link.description:
What to open in the browser to sign it in, once, before `link_expires_at`: the page, with the code after a `#`, which
a browser keeps to itself and never sends to the server.

warnings.description:
Things the owner should know about what this viewer will see, such as a layout the page is set not to show. The viewer is
made all the same.

WindowState.description: Whether displays can ask to join right now.

open.description:
Whether the window is open. While it is, a display that has not joined can ask to, and a display that lost
its key can ask to take its name back. Closed, those requests are turned away; a display already waiting
can still be approved.

closes_at.description: When the window closes by itself. Only present while it is open.
